stories.title: Kim Jong Un inspects new naval base as North Korea pushes to expand maritime power
stories.standfirst: State media said the North Korean leader toured a major base under construction on the east coast and ordered it finished on schedule.
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected a large naval base being built on the country's east coast and ordered its timely completion, state-run media reported on Thursday. The visit is the latest signal that Pyongyang intends to expand its naval reach alongside its missile and nuclear programmes.
stories.imageCaption: North Korean state media published images of Kim Jong Un touring a naval base under construction on the east coast.
body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has inspected a major naval base under construction on the country's east coast and ordered that it be completed on time, according to state-run media reports carried by UPI on Thursday.

The inspection is the latest in a series of visits to military sites this year, and it points to an effort to pair the country's missile and nuclear programmes with a more capable surface and submarine fleet.

Details of the base's size, cost or operational timeline were not disclosed in the state media account. Independent verification of the visit is not possible, as North Korea does not permit unrestricted access for foreign journalists to military sites.
Analysts have long noted that a modernised east-coast naval facility would give Pyongyang a shorter route into open water and a more dispersed basing posture for its submarines.
The report comes as regional navies step up exercises and as diplomatic contacts between Pyongyang and Washington remain limited.

stories.title: DRC opposition vows to resist constitutional changes under Tshisekedi
stories.standfirst: A new law easing the rules for a referendum has been condemned by opposition parties as an attempt to extend the president's hold on power.
stories.summary: President Félix Tshisekedi has enacted a law that eases the conditions for holding a referendum on constitutional matters in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Opposition parties, including the C64 coalition, say the change is designed to let him seek a third term and have vowed to resist it.
stories.imageCaption: DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi enacted a law paving the way for constitutional change, condemned by the opposition as an attempt to cling to power.
body: The Democratic Republic of Congo's opposition has condemned a new law enacted by President Félix Tshisekedi that opens the door to constitutional changes, accusing him of seeking to extend his hold on power.

"He openly declares that he wants to stay in power until someone strong enough can drive him out," said Jean-Baptiste Kasekwa, an opposition politician and member of the C64 coalition, which brings together the country's main opposition parties.
The law, announced in an order read on national television overnight between Tuesday and Wednesday, eases the rules around holding a referendum on constitutional matters.

It comes two years ahead of the next scheduled elections, and with the reformed M23 armed group — now led by Tshisekedi's predecessor Joseph Kabila — vowing to "put an end to tyranny", by force if needed.
Tshisekedi has previously said he would accept a third term if voters wanted him to run again. The opposition has vowed to resist any constitutional change.
"I think this is an announcement or a decision that does not help to ease tensions. On the contrary, it adds fuel to the fire," one opposition figure said, according to Africanews.

stories.title: Coalition talks under way across South Africa's major metros after local elections
stories.standfirst: Seven of the country's eight biggest metros have no outright winner, and councils must be constituted within 14 days.
stories.summary: Coalition negotiations are under way in South Africa's largest cities after the 2026 local government elections left seven of eight major metros without an outright winner. The 14-day window to constitute municipal councils opened on 11 November following the gazetting of results, with Cape Town the only metro where the DA won a majority.
stories.imageCaption: Coalition talks are under way in South Africa's major metros following the 2026 local government elections.
body: Coalition talks are under way across South Africa's major metros and municipalities following the 2026 local government elections, SABC News reported on Thursday.
The 14-day period for the constitution of municipal councils began on Wednesday, 11 November, following the official gazetting of the election results.
Seven out of the eight major metros have been left without an outright winner. Cape Town is the only metro where the Democratic Alliance secured an outright majority.
The South African Local Government Association has urged parties to prioritise stability and transparent governance as negotiations continue.
How the talks resolve will shape service delivery in the country's economic centres for the next council term.

stories.title: Tinubu seeks Reps' approval for N10.79tn external borrowing
stories.standfirst: The request covers the external borrowing already written into the 2026 Appropriation Act — about $7.7bn at the budget exchange rate.
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to approve implementation of the N10.79 trillion external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The sum, about $7.7 billion at the N1,400 budget rate, is part of the N29.218 trillion borrowing already provided for to part-finance the deficit.
stories.imageCaption: President Bola Tinubu's letter was read on the floor of the House of Representatives by Speaker Tajudeen Abbas.
body: President Bola Tinubu is seeking the statutory authorisation of the House of Representatives to implement the N10.79 trillion external borrowing approved in the 2026 Appropriation Act.

In a letter read by the Speaker, Tajudeen Abbas, the President asked the House to approve the plan so the government can raise the funds through one or more sources — conventional and commercial facilities from multilateral and bilateral institutions, the International Monetary Fund, bridge financing and direct borrowing, with emphasis on Eurobonds.

"I write to request the permission of the House of Representatives to implement the new external borrowing plan contained in the 2026 Appropriation Act in the sum of N10,790,366,835,481, which is equivalent to 7,707,404,882.49 dollars at the budget exchange rate of USD 1 to N1,400 for the part financing of the budget deficit of N29.218 trillion," the letter stated.
The President explained that the borrowing was divided into N18.28 trillion in domestic loans and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing.

The request concerns the legally required approval of borrowing terms rather than authorisation for new borrowing, and the funds are earmarked for projects in defence, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health.

stories.title: INEC removes 1.6 million invalid voter records, identifies 54 officials over registration fraud
stories.standfirst: The commission is cleaning the register ahead of the 2027 general election and has begun training state officials.
stories.summary: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission has removed 1.6 million invalid voter records and identified 54 officials in connection with registration fraud. The clean-up comes as INEC trains heads of departments in state offices and the FCT ahead of the 2027 general election.
stories.imageCaption: INEC headquarters in Abuja. The commission says it has removed 1.6 million invalid entries from the voter register.
body: Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission has removed 1.6 million invalid voter records and identified 54 officials over registration fraud, The Nigerian Observer reported.
The clean-up of the register is one of the commission's central tasks before the 2027 general election, when Nigerians will choose a president, national assembly members and state governors.
Separately, INEC has commenced a three-day capacity-building workshop for Heads of Departments in its state offices and the Federal Capital Territory to strengthen preparations for the 2027 vote.

The commission has not published a full breakdown of the invalid records or the status of the officials identified. JagX Pulse has not independently verified the figures beyond the commission's published account.
Election observers have repeatedly called for a more transparent register audit process in the run-up to the vote.

stories.title: Dangote Refinery lifts output to 700,000bpd as it chases 1.4 million bpd
stories.standfirst: The Lagos plant says it wants to more than double capacity within 30 months and become the world's largest single-train refinery.
stories.summary: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has raised crude processing to 700,000 barrels per day and is targeting 1.4 million bpd within 30 months. The company says the expansion would make it the largest refinery globally and cut Nigeria's reliance on imported refined products.
stories.imageCaption: The Dangote refinery at Lekki, Lagos. The plant is ramping up crude processing toward a 1.4 million bpd target.
body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has increased crude oil processing to 700,000 barrels per day and is targeting 1.4 million bpd within the next 30 months, according to The Guardian Nigeria.

Devakumar Edwin, Vice-President for oil and gas at Dangote Industries Limited, described the ramp-up as part of a strategy to more than double capacity and position the facility as potentially the largest refinery globally.
Aliko Dangote has outlined plans to make the plant the world's largest refinery by 2028, with a processing capacity of 1.4 million barrels per day.
The company says the expansion is expected to boost Nigeria's energy self-sufficiency, reduce dependence on imported refined products and strengthen the country's position as a regional export hub.
The refinery has also set a target of 12 million tonnes of fertiliser output by 2030, according to company statements reported in Nigerian media.

stories.title: Senate moves to summon NCC, MTN, Glo over alleged unjustified deductions
stories.standfirst: Lawmakers want the regulator and operators to answer complaints about unexplained charges on subscriber accounts.
stories.summary: Nigeria's Senate has mandated a committee to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission, MTN, Globacom and others over complaints of alleged unjustified deductions from subscribers. The move puts consumer protection in telecoms back on the legislative agenda.
stories.imageCaption: Nigeria's Senate wants the telecoms regulator and operators to answer subscriber complaints about unexplained charges.
body: Nigeria's Senate has mandated one of its committees to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission, MTN, Globacom and other operators over allegations of unjustified deductions from subscribers, Daily Nigerian reported.
The resolution follows complaints from consumers about charges they say were applied without clear explanation or consent.
The NCC is the sector regulator responsible for tariff oversight and consumer protection in Nigeria's telecoms market, one of the largest in Africa by subscriber numbers.
The committee's terms of reference and hearing date were not immediately published. JagX Pulse will update this story when they are.
Telecoms operators have previously said most deductions relate to value-added services that subscribers opt into, a claim consumer groups dispute.

stories.title: Meta returns to Kenya's High Court over hate speech in Ethiopia
stories.standfirst: The case tests whether platform moderation failures abroad can be litigated in African courts.
stories.summary: Meta is back before Kenya's High Court in a case concerning hate speech and content moderation in Ethiopia. The proceedings are being watched as a test of whether African courts can hold global platforms accountable for harms outside their home jurisdictions.
stories.imageCaption: Meta is facing renewed litigation in Kenya's High Court over content moderation and hate speech in Ethiopia.
body: Meta has returned to Kenya's High Court in a case concerning hate speech and content moderation in Ethiopia, Tech Policy Press reported on 11 November.

The litigation is part of a wider push by researchers, activists and lawyers to establish that global platforms owe duties to users in the countries where their products are used, not only where they are headquartered.
Kenya has become a significant venue for such cases because Meta and other platforms employ large moderation and content-review operations in Nairobi.
The company has previously said it invests heavily in safety systems and local-language moderation, while acknowledging that enforcement is imperfect at scale.
A ruling in the case could influence how other African jurisdictions approach platform liability. No judgment date has been announced.

stories.title: Flamingos make history with Nigeria's first U-17 Women's World Cup title
stories.standfirst: Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in Rabat to win the tournament for the first time — after losing their opening match.
stories.summary: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in Rabat on 7 November to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, the country's first title in the women's competition. The win takes Nigeria's combined U-17 World Cup tally to six and makes them the first African country to complete the double.
stories.imageCaption: Flamingos captain Chidi Harmony with the U-17 Women's World Cup trophy after Nigeria beat Japan 2-1 in Rabat.
body: Nigeria's Flamingos made history on Saturday, 7 November, beating Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Rabat, Morocco.

It was Nigeria's first title in the women's competition. Combined with the country's successes in the men's U-17 tournament, the victory takes Nigeria's total number of FIFA U-17 World Cup titles across both competitions to six — the first African country to complete the double.

The Flamingos also became the first team to win the U-17 Women's World Cup after losing their opening match, having started the campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Poland in the group stage. They responded with six consecutive victories to reach the final and lift the trophy.
Captain Chidi Harmony lifted the trophy in Rabat, and the team returned to a wave of congratulatory messages from across Nigeria.
The Nigerian Senate has since approved a N100 million reward for the squad, and President Bola Tinubu has also announced a gift to the players.

stories.title: Latin Grammy Awards return to Las Vegas for 2026 ceremony
stories.standfirst: Latin music's biggest night takes place at the MGM Grand Garden Arena, with the show starting at 5pm local time.
stories.summary: The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are being held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on 12 November. The ceremony honours achievements across Latin music, with live performances and awards across dozens of categories.
stories.imageCaption: The Latin Grammy Awards return to the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas for the 2026 ceremony.
body: The 2026 Latin Grammy Awards are being held at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday, 12 November, the Associated Press reported.
The ceremony, organised by the Latin Recording Academy, honours excellence in Latin music across dozens of categories and genres, and is one of the largest nights in the Latin music calendar.
The show is scheduled to begin at 5pm local time in Las Vegas, which is 2am West Africa Time on Friday, 13 November.
The awards return to Las Vegas, a city with a long association with the ceremony, and are expected to draw a large contingent of artists, industry executives and fans to the Strip.
JagX Pulse has not independently confirmed the full performer line-up or the complete list of nominees for this edition.

stories.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient and starts 42-day countdown to disease-free status
stories.standfirst: Health Minister Aden Duale said prevention measures will continue until 23 December.
stories.summary: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, beginning a 42-day countdown before the country can be declared free of the disease. Health Minister Aden Duale announced the milestone in Nairobi on 11 November, more than five weeks after Kenya recorded its first case on 6 October.
stories.imageCaption: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale announces the discharge of the country's last Ebola patient in Nairobi.
body: Kenya has released its last Ebola patient and begun a 42-day countdown to be declared free of the disease, Health Minister Aden Duale announced at a news conference in Nairobi on Wednesday, 11 November.
The milestone came more than five weeks after the country recorded its first case on 6 October. Kenya will continue to exercise prevention measures until 23 December, Duale said.
The minister praised the country's response, saying Kenya had reported early, published its figures and shared its data while keeping its borders open as international health regulations require.

Cases across the wider region have surpassed 11,000 since the outbreak began in May, according to figures cited by Africanews. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has said the outbreak is not yet under control because the source of more than 80% of new cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo is still unknown.
The 42-day window is the standard period used to confirm that transmission has stopped, covering two incubation cycles of the virus.

stories.title: WHO publishes updated estimates of the global burden of foodborne disease
stories.standfirst: The report covers 2000–2021 and sets out how much illness and death is linked to contaminated food worldwide.
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has published updated estimates of the global burden of foodborne diseases for the period 2000 to 2021. The report is part of WHO's effort to quantify how contaminated food affects health systems and economies, particularly in lower-income countries.
stories.imageCaption: The World Health Organization published updated global estimates of foodborne disease burden for 2000–2021.
body: The World Health Organization has published updated estimates of the global burden of foodborne diseases covering the period 2000 to 2021.
The report presents key findings on how contaminated food contributes to illness and death worldwide, and is intended to help countries prioritise food safety investment.
WHO has previously estimated that unsafe food causes hundreds of millions of cases of illness each year, with children under five disproportionately affected.
The organisation published the report on 4 November 2026 alongside other updates on neglected tropical diseases and primary health care for displaced populations.
JagX Pulse has not reproduced the report's specific mortality and morbidity figures, which are set out in the full document on WHO's website.

stories.title: "Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs": Guterres opens COP31 with blunt warning
stories.standfirst: The UN chief told leaders in Antalya that the climate crisis is outrunning the world and accused the fossil fuel lobby of delaying action.
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told the COP31 Leaders' Summit in Antalya, Türkiye, that fossil fuels must be phased out and that the industry's lobbying is slowing climate action. He said emissions reached all-time highs in 2025 and that heat records keep breaking.
stories.imageCaption: UN Secretary-General António Guterres speaks at the COP31 Leaders' Summit in Antalya, Türkiye, on 11 November 2026.
body: UN Secretary-General António Guterres delivered one of his sharpest attacks on the fossil fuel industry at the COP31 Leaders' Summit in Antalya, Türkiye, on 11 November.
"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. Emissions in 2025 reached all-time highs. Heat records keep shattering," Guterres said.
"Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won't happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do," he added.

COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 in Antalya, with Türkiye's Murat Kurum as conference president and Australia's Chris Bowen as president of negotiations. The summit's stated aim is to move from pledges to implementation of existing commitments.

Finland used the summit to announce concrete plans to phase out fossil fuels, becoming the fourth country to do so after France, Germany and the Netherlands. Several senior European leaders, including France's Emmanuel Macron and Germany's Friedrich Merz, were absent from the leaders' segment.

A second global stocktake — the inventory check of progress toward the Paris Agreement's goals — begins at COP31, even as the IPCC has yet to agree a timetable for its next round of working-group reports.
